newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - Sterling on election date news.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Sterling on election date news.

text.p: Following is a selection of currency analysts' reactions to news on Monday that UK Prime Minister John Major called an election for May 1.
PAUL MEGGYESI, SENIOR CURRENCY ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL

"We have expected this for a long time, so it should be neutral for sterling. There is no real uncertainty about the election outcome because economic policy under a Labour government would not be that different. Today's sterling weakness coincides with the annoucement but the sell-off is a convenient excuse for some long overdue profit-taking as the market begins to realise that the pound isn't really supported by interest rate arguments."
BRIAN MARTIN, CHIEF ECONOMIST FOREX, BZW:

"People have had an excellent run on sterling. We can probably now expect some more profit-taking on long sterling positions into the election. It's not the election itself that's such a problem for sterling but some growing worries about the initial policy mix under a Labour government."
DAVID BROWN, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT BEAR STEARNS:

"The market's traditional knee-jerk reaction is to always sell off on news of an impending general election. But it also has to be put into perspective of the stronger mark in Europe at the moment. Sterling is buckling under a generally rampant German mark, and news of a general election on the cards does not help its case."
ROGER FRANCIS, SENIOR ANALYST, IBJ INTERNATIONAL:

"It's confirmation of a date everyone was expecting. It's hard to see anyone getting upset or surprised about the date or any good reason to be upset about the likely outcome. If anything, (a Labour victory) could be a mild positive for sterling. Labour looks to be willing to keep tight fiscal and monetary policy in the near-term, and maybe more accomodative to (European) monetary union."
